claims.text: Introducing a ductile phase reinforcement through secondary processing will overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
Introducing the ductile phase will retain or increase the strength of the eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure comprising dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy exhibits limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
The proposed intervention is addition of 5 vol% pure Ni or Cu by powder metallurgy followed by hot isostatic pressing at 900°C for 2 hours.
The proposed treatment is applicable to room-temperature tensile loading at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The introduced ductile phases will act as barriers to dislocation movement.
The introduced ductile phases will reduce dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
The ductile phase will provide alternative deformation pathways and promote plastic deformation.
The alternative deformation pathways will reduce local stress concentrations and microcracking.
The treatment will increase tensile ductility by 30%, from 5% to 6.5%.
The treatment will increase yield strength by 10%, from 800 MPa to 880 MPa.
The reinforcement may reduce but not completely eliminate microcracking and catastrophic damage during straining.
The optimal reinforcement volume fraction, reinforcement distribution, and processing conditions remain to be determined.
